name: Chlorpyrifos
first_aid: Move to fresh air, remove contaminated clothes, wash skin and hair with soap and water, rinse eyes for 15 minutes if exposed, and seek urgent medical help.
notes: Organophosphates can affect nerves. Severe symptoms need immediate care.

name: Malathion
first_aid: Stop exposure, wash thoroughly, rinse eyes if needed, and call a doctor or poison control if symptoms occur.
notes: Risk rises with concentrated product or repeated exposure.

name: Parathion
first_aid: This is highly dangerous. Decontaminate quickly and get emergency medical care immediately.
notes: Very toxic organophosphate. Do not wait for symptoms.

name: Diazinon
first_aid: Remove from exposure, wash skin and hair, rinse eyes, and seek medical help for any nerve-type symptoms.
notes: Can cause cholinergic poisoning.

name: Dimethoate
first_aid: Remove contaminated clothing, wash skin, move to fresh air, and call poison control or emergency care.
notes: Common agricultural organophosphate.

name: Monocrotophos
first_aid: Treat as an emergency. Decontaminate and go to hospital immediately with the label.
notes: Highly hazardous pesticide.

name: Carbaryl
first_aid: Wash exposed skin, rinse eyes, move to fresh air, and seek care if symptoms continue.
notes: Carbamates can cause symptoms similar to organophosphates.

name: Carbofuran
first_aid: Emergency medical care is needed. Remove contaminated clothing and wash exposed skin immediately.
notes: Highly toxic carbamate.

name: Methomyl
first_aid: Decontaminate and get medical help if any symptoms occur.
notes: Rapid onset symptoms are possible.

name: Cypermethrin
first_aid: Wash skin with soap and water. Rinse eyes for 15 minutes. Move to fresh air if spray was inhaled.
notes: Often causes skin tingling or burning sensations.

name: Permethrin
first_aid: Remove contaminated clothing and wash exposed skin. Rinse eyes if exposed.
notes: Concentrates can irritate skin and eyes.

name: Deltamethrin
first_aid: Wash skin and hair. Rinse eyes with water. Seek help if symptoms are severe.
notes: Avoid scrubbing irritated skin.

name: Imidacloprid
first_aid: Wash exposed areas and call poison control if swallowed or if symptoms appear.
notes: Bring the product label to medical care.

name: Acetamiprid
first_aid: Stop exposure, wash, rinse eyes, and seek medical advice for persistent symptoms.
notes: Follow label precautions closely.

name: Glyphosate
first_aid: Wash skin, rinse eyes for 15 minutes, and get medical help if swallowed or symptoms continue.
notes: Formulations vary; surfactants can increase irritation.

name: Paraquat
first_aid: Emergency. Do not induce vomiting. Remove contaminated clothes, wash skin, and go to hospital immediately.
notes: Paraquat can be fatal, especially if swallowed.

name: 2,4-D
first_aid: Wash skin, rinse eyes, move to fresh air, and seek advice if swallowed or symptomatic.
notes: Avoid repeated skin contact.

name: Atrazine
first_aid: Wash exposed skin and rinse eyes. Seek help if symptoms persist.
notes: Use PPE during mixing and spraying.

name: Mancozeb
first_aid: Remove contaminated clothing, wash skin, rinse eyes, and move to fresh air.
notes: Dust can irritate airways.

name: Copper sulfate
first_aid: Rinse eyes, wash skin, and seek medical help if swallowed.
notes: Can be corrosive in concentrated forms.

name: Sulfur
first_aid: Wash skin, rinse eyes, and move to fresh air.
notes: Dust exposure is a common irritation risk.

name: Captan
first_aid: Wash exposed skin and rinse eyes with clean water.
notes: May irritate skin and mucous membranes.

name: Aluminium phosphide
first_aid: Emergency. Move to fresh air only if safe and call emergency medical help immediately.
notes: Releases phosphine gas. Do not attempt rescue without protection in enclosed spaces.

name: Zinc phosphide
first_aid: Do not induce vomiting. Get emergency medical care and carry the label.
notes: Can release toxic phosphine gas after ingestion.

name: Brodifacoum
first_aid: Wash skin if exposed and seek medical advice immediately if swallowed or bleeding occurs.
notes: Symptoms can be delayed. Medical treatment may require vitamin K under supervision.

name: Warfarin
first_aid: Call poison control or a doctor if swallowed. Watch for delayed bleeding.
notes: Do not self-treat with medicine.

name: Endosulfan
first_aid: Emergency medical help is needed. Remove contaminated clothing and wash skin immediately.
notes: Highly hazardous and banned or restricted in many places.

name: Lindane
first_aid: Wash exposed skin and seek urgent medical care for neurological symptoms.
notes: Can affect the nervous system.

name: Fipronil
first_aid: Wash skin, rinse eyes, and get medical advice if swallowed or symptomatic.
notes: Avoid repeated exposure.

name: Abamectin
first_aid: Decontaminate and seek medical advice quickly if symptoms occur.
notes: Concentrates can be dangerous.
